assumptions.text: No source code detected in /workspace/skill-marketplace/ddd-smoke-workspace and no stack named in README / manifest / understand constraints; language left 'undecided' and module paths kept neutral rather than inferred, because a language is baked into every path in this artifact
Persistence not detected; adapters assume postgres
Module paths are language-neutral (src/<context>) until the language is named (single deployable layout)

Clock commands are driving ports invoked by a scheduler adapter (connect N1, organise N1), not webhooks; the skeleton's <Context>Callbacks / ClockWebhookHandler entries were renamed to a SchedulerAdapter on <Context>Commands.
Only the loan aggregate carries transactional invariants; reservation is a small second aggregate (one hold per item) so a hold and a loan never share a transaction.
send-due-reminders is an application service over the loans-due read model (no aggregate state changes; it emits due-reminder-sent per loan), handled_by transaction-script.

The skeleton's generic EmailGateway / MembershipGateway / FeesGateway ports on lending were removed as duplicates of the purpose-named DueNoticeGateway / MembershipStatusGateway / FeeBalanceGateway (spotted on diagrams/aggregates-lending.png).

open_questions.text: Name the implementation language, framework and persistence. Nothing upstream states them and they were deliberately not inferred: every module path, port name and test name in this plan depends on the answer

Should the membership fee card charge reuse fees' StripeGateway port directly (one adapter package imported by two modules) or should membership call fees' PayFee use case? The plan assumes the shared adapter package.

aggregates.name: Reservation
invariants: At most one live reservation exists per item
A reservation expires exactly 48 hours after it was placed

aggregates.name: Loan
invariants: A loan is renewed at most once, and only while no other member holds a reservation on the item
A loan's due date is 14 days after check-out, plus 7 if renewed
A returned loan cannot be renewed, marked overdue or returned again
A loan is created only when BorrowEligibility allowed it at that instant

plain_words.what: We turned the design into a build plan: which module holds which rules, what talks to what through named 'ports', and which tests to write first.
plain_words.decided: Four modules in one program. Lending gets two proper domain objects (Loan with 4 invariants, Reservation with 2); the other three are simple records and scripts. 5 slices, lending first.
plain_words.assumed: That the nightly jobs are just functions a scheduler calls, so it does not matter yet who schedules them (organise D1 is open).
plain_words.riskiest: No programming language, framework or database has been named. We refused to guess: every path here is neutral, and the plan cannot be started until someone answers that one question.
